column1: # The latest independent audit of each table: an auditor who did not write the entries drew a random sample of rows graded understood
# and re-derived each from the binaries or the cited specification. real = the entry held up, shallow = true but derived from a name or
# credited without behaviour of its own, wrong = contradicted. sample is small: read it with the percentage. The last row of a table with
# the latest date is the one summary.tsv and docs/coverage.md show.

column7: sample of the routine rows and second-bank copies added since the seed review (seed 20261102); each disassembled from the 1.44.0 Origin 300 body and the relocated copies compared byte for byte; every claimed argument, call, store and literal held
general_req_war_flag in the 2 MB package and the L2 partition task's brick lookup, both read from the handler through the flag or database call to the reply record
the chip-select 3 control write of the USB slot setup: value, address and offset read in the image, register name checked against the public chip map
the Linux L1 package of 1.44.0: kernel release and every cramfs entry count re-derived by walking the image (both Linux packages agree)

the on-chip peripherals note and the USB controller register note held; the 2 MB package comparison said the request task initialiser differs between the 1 MB and 2 MB packages when the pairing had split one routine (package 1 has the same guard, semaphore and registration); corrected

twenty of the 25 open-question entries drawn at random and re-derived from the image and the carved L2 tree: addresses, counts, callers and string literals held for 17; three were shallow (the USB part route pointed at a host-side driver that cannot name controller silicon, the routine at 0xffe48370 is a 28-byte wrapper and the entry asked to read it, and the writers of settings 9 and 0x10 were already locatable); the guard-word entry put the peer initializer's entry at the wrong address; fixed

twenty of the 636 rows of the two L1 request tables drawn at random (seed 20261102; ten per table); each code-to-handler address re-derived by tracing the compare chain with a separate interpreter and each text claim by re-decoding the handler with its own bounds (all addresses, line counts and same, RAM-only or changed classifications held); three were shallow because the compared text is only a short setup stub that branches into shared code, which the page caveated for one code in one set only; the page now says so for every set

twenty changed items of the L2 user-space note and its table rows drawn at random (seed 20261102) from the 34 statements and tables the three commits touched; each re-derived by decoding the kernel driver, the daemon, the GUI, the partition task and the system libraries of the 1.44.0 tree with a separate decoder, and the unpack steps and image table re-run on all thirteen images; 10 held (device-node and ioctl numbers, kernel read semantics, touch port settings, flash window, handshake bytes, frame writer, socket reader, byte patterns, revision value, reset ioctl semantics); 4 shallow (the slot node row listed a record ioctl that belongs to the control node, the open row missed the busy error, the serial row stated a speed the note says is not established, the partition code 7 row was unconditional); 6 wrong: the operator ports are one opened path not two, the reset test is revision above 0 so revision 1 is not the old path, the slot-record query goes to the control node, the USB path filter compares the form without the device number and any prefix matches, the frame reader does not grow its buffer in the daemon use but reports -701, and the device record name used for filtering omitted the form split; the sampled rate was under 85 percent so every other changed statement was re-checked, which also found the entry counts off by one; all corrected in this commit and the one before it

twenty of the 583 call sites of the L1 console and log sinks drawn at random (seed 20261102; 19 table rows plus one curated role in place of a duplicate draw), each re-derived from the 1.44.0 listing and image: call address, severity, file, line, format, pushed arguments and guard. Seventeen held. One was shallow (the table dropped an argument pushed before a nested call, so a two-argument format showed one). Two were wrong: a role said the status text was printed when the format has no conversion for it and the first argument is the monitor record name, and a guard row named flags from the wrong instruction and a branch that does not control the call. All 24 curated roles were then re-read: a role that said the pre-power check returned zero (it prints on a nonzero result), and four roles that restated the format instead of the range or switch condition, were corrected; the extractor now counts arguments from the call's own cleanup, reads subq and addq as flag setters, and notes other paths into a call

twenty changed items of the ARM L1 helper, serial and flash, and boot-script notes and of the ColdFire request-handler notes and request-code table drawn at random (seed 20261102; 11 ARM, 9 ColdFire) and re-derived by decoding the 1.48.1 ARM programs and the 1.44.0 ColdFire packages with a separate decoder: addresses, constants, compare values, call targets, jump tables, record offsets and string literals held for 18; the NAND bad-block tool was wrong (its argument is a summary flag, not a partition selector, and it scans 32 pages per block testing spare byte 5, not the first pages) and the YAFFS repair tool left its two-pattern block test unread (shallow); both rewritten, with a script-count slip, a missing netwatch start and a reset monitor size also corrected; every routine address and size the two ARM notes give for the l1 program was also checked against its exported symbol table and agreed

twenty changed items of the host-tool, version-comparison and callback-pointer notes drawn at random (seed 20261102) from the 41 statements and table rows the three commits touched; each re-derived from the ColdFire packages of the 1.44.0 and 1.48.1 sets with a separate decoder, the L2 tree carved from 1.48.0, and the MIPS host tools disassembled (callback RAM words, copy sources, flash words and empty routines, per-package differing byte counts and positions, bank record sums, relocation table entries, library imports, the text-command request, the reboot case, the sequence match, the error byte, the l2cmd byte comparison, the flashsc option strings and the validate request); 19 held; 1 shallow (the flashsc refusal for an L1 binary stated as a requirement that both images and relocation tables be present, while the shipped text says it lacks both the images and the tables and the selecting test was not located; reworded). Outside the sample: the package 1 row of the byte-difference table named fewer sites than the bytes show, the library export count was called functions though 43 of the 253 are data, and bank record word 7 was still listed unknown in the record table though every record sums to zero; all corrected

8 changed items of the L2 user-space and L1 chunk notes drawn at random (seed 20261102) from the statements and table rows the recent commits added, re-derived from the 1.44.0 L2 daemon and libraries and the L1 package 1 bytes with a separate PowerPC and ColdFire decoder: the dhcpserver NVRAM key and messages, the power-queue step arguments, the flash probe and erase-poll rules, the date command result handling and its time zone setting, the 0x3001 buffer allocation, the 0x3003 count and payload checks, the open-message reply and free, and the /dev/snsc strings; all held. Two further drawn items (the slot clearing call in the 0x3001 path, whose target is an unresolved address in the image, and an open-question entry) were unsure and are not counted; a stronger review is needed for them

targeted re-check of one note item, not a random sample: the start-frame slot clear in the 0x3001 path, which the notes graded as established. Its call target was read as 0xaaaaaaaa, a decode artifact of a range cut mid-instruction; the real target is inside a copy routine, so the clear is not established and the note was reworded to unknown. The other items of the 2026-11-02 row were not re-read in this pass
